questions.q: What question does a business unit answer?
options: Which chart of accounts is used
Which operational entity a transaction was processed under
Which currency a journal is stored in
Which accounting period is open
questions.explain: A business unit is the operational boundary — which office, division, or operating company a transaction belongs to.

questions.q: What are the "four Cs" that define a ledger?
options: Currency, Chart of accounts, Calendar, Convention
Customer, Contact, Contract, Credit
Company, Country, City, Code
Control, Compliance, Close, Confirm
questions.explain: A ledger is defined by its chart of accounts, accounting calendar, functional currency, and accounting convention/method.

questions.q: Which table represents ledger definitions in the Oracle Fusion data model?
options: AP_INVOICES_ALL
HZ_PARTIES
GL_LEDGERS
XLA_EVENTS
questions.explain: GL_LEDGERS stores ledger definitions, including the PRIMARY_LEDGER_ID column secondary ledgers use to point back to their primary ledger.

questions.q: How can business units and ledgers relate to each other?
options: They must always match exactly one-to-one
A ledger can never serve more than one business unit
Multiple business units can post into the same shared ledger, while each business unit has one primary ledger
Business units and ledgers have no relationship at all
questions.explain: Several business units commonly share one ledger, but each business unit is assigned one primary ledger for its own transactions.

questions.q: Why is it useful to keep business-unit security and ledger data access conceptually separate?
options: Because they are enforced by the exact same mechanism, so distinguishing them is purely academic
Because a user's subledger transaction access (by business unit) and their General Ledger reporting access (by data access set) can be scoped differently
Because ledgers have no security model at all
Because business units only apply to Fixed Assets
questions.explain: Oracle Fusion secures subledger transactions by business unit and secures GL viewing/reporting access separately through data access sets, so the two can be scoped very differently for the same user.
